newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian PM Howard attacks Hanson protesters.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM Howard attacks Hanson protesters.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday that violent protests against race row politician Pauline Hanson and her One Nation party were counter-productive.
Howard said rowdy protests at two launches of the One Nation party earlier this week only served to publicise Hanson's extremist views on immigration and Aborigines.
"Their (the protesters') behaviour is worse than the behaviour of some of the people they attack," said Howard in an interview on a Sydney radio station.
"I think those demonstrations at her rallies are counter-productive. If they think they are damaging the cause against which they're demonstrating, they're wrong," he said.
"These thugs who are trying to bust up all these meetings are really helping her, they're not harming her."
Police blamed a small group of militant protesters for violence at a One Nation meeting in the Victorian rural town of Dandenong on Monday night.
The protesters threw urine-filled balloons and eggs and attacked pro-Hanson supporters, leaving one elderly man with a fractured skull.
"It doesn't matter what people may think of Ms Hanson's views. She's got a right to put her views and people have got a right to go along and hear them," Howard said.
Howard's education minister, Amanda Vanstone, attacked Hanson, labelling her comments as "mad rantings" and said her party had been infiltrated by far right wing racists.
Vanstone warned that Hanson could harm Australia's A$3.0 billion (US$2.2 billion) export education industry, which attracts primarily Asian students to courses in Australia.
"It would be an absolute tragedy if the numbers of international students coming to Australia reduced as a result of this woman's mad rantings," Vanstone said.

"Pauline's pinhead policies such as restricting foreign investment and restoring tariff barriers would throw Australia right out of the global ball game. The woman needs to get a grip on the 21st century and Australia's place in the global community."
Howard has been criticised by former prime ministers, human rights officials and ethnic leaders for not strongly repudiating Hanson and allowing the bitter race debate to simmer on.
But on Thursday, Howard again rejected such criticism, defending Australia as a tolerant nation.
"We can be proud of the record of tolerance in this country and I think most Australians are sick to death of being told every day they are a bunch of racists," Howard said.
